description: e2000fs_calib11_metricgn. Heuristic-free successor of e2000fs_calib_point4_144h: the objective is the board key's own gradient, and the level enters by identity instead of by regression. (A) Metric-derived sample weights. The key is S = mean_lead sqrt(RMSE_l*TRMSE_l), so S^4 ~ MSE_l*TIMSE_l per lead. The onboarding TIMSE formula decomposes EXACTLY into per-observation weights, TIMSE_l = sum_i a_il e_i^2 with a_il = (1/R) sum_{k: q_k<=y_i} dq_k/N_k (k over the 100 percentile thresholds, N_k the exceedance count, R = v_max-v_min), so dS ~ e_i[1 + rho_l (N a_i)] and one weighted squared-error fit satisfies the first-order condition. rho_l = MSE_l/TIMSE_l is a dimensionless scalar measured on a strictly prior calibration block (the last 25% of the training window, predicted by the parent recipe fitted on the earlier 75%); a_il is a property of the training labels and needs no predictions. Nothing is hand-set: the parent's 4x sample weight above 550 km/s and its 550 threshold do not appear anywhere in training or prediction, and the weights are smooth in the label (about 1.05x at the median, 1.2x at the 90th percentile, 10-25x at the 99th, the log-survival shape the metric implies) rather than a step. (B) Anchor-residual target. The label is y - v_lag0 and the anchor is added back at prediction time (the tree analogue of reversible instance normalisation, algebraically a base_margin offset), so level enters by identity; this removes the h1-h3 regression below persistence and the level-induced amplitude compression of the parent. The population estimator this targets is E[w(Y)Y|x]/E[w(Y)|x], the probability-weighted mixture of conditional tail means that TIMSE minimises, not the conditional mean plain squared error minimises. Everything else is the frozen parent recipe: three 24-h vector-leaf XGBoost boosters per period on the 237-column Top30 design, 900 rounds, depth 3, eta 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.7, min_child_weight 20, lambda 5, seed 42. One booster per horizon block, no routing, no gate, no blend, no post-processing. Development trio one year before F1 (D1/D2/D3 2025, pre-cutoff): S 116.187 -> 108.604 (-6.5%), TIMSE -20.7%, RMSE -1.7%. Refit on the F1/F2/F3 quarters with cutoffs 2025-12-29 / 2026-03-29 / 2026-06-29 and 72 h target maturity; all 6,315 origins forecast unconditionally.

data.feature_set: df.parquet Top30 (21 constant + 24 h x 9 varying per block), unchanged from the parent

objective.family: squared error with metric-derived per-(row, lead) sample weights
objective.weights: w_il = 1 + rho_l * (N a_il); a_il is the exact decomposition of onboarding TIMSE (a_il = (1/R) sum_{k: q_k<=y_i} dq_k/N_k), N a_il dimensionless
objective.rho_source: rho_l = MSE_l/TIMSE_l of the parent recipe on the last 25% of the training window (calibration block), fitted on the earlier 75%; scikit-learn cross-fitting rationale
objective.estimand: E[w(Y)Y|x]/E[w(Y)|x] = probability-weighted mixture of conditional tail means
objective.no_hand_set_constants: rho_l is measured from data; a_il is a property of the labels

target.form: y - v_lag0 (anchor-residual); anchor added back at prediction time
target.equivalent_to: XGBoost base_margin offset; tree analogue of reversible instance normalisation
target.reference: Kim et al. 2022 (RevIN, ICLR); residual/baseline targets, FPP2 3.1

hyperparameters.post_processing: none (no clipping, no calibration lane, no blend)
